item.title: Verbose beta 316
item.description:
Five keyboard languages and settled details

Mac

  • Settings icons sit on a neutral square with an ink glyph. Settings no longer borrows the capture colors, so persimmon always means Record and butter Dictate. Delete rows keep their red glyph and word.
  • Side card labels and the line over each page's title are in sentence case. Today, Recent questions, Selected, and the date over Home's greeting match the rest of the app, in the same small style as Settings' group labels.
  • Home's side column drops Dictations, and the Library's drops Collections. Both repeated the sidebar. With This week, thoughts, and Journal hidden, Home uses the full width; with the inspector open, so does the Library's table.
  • In the welcome tour, Return goes to the next step at once. A click still slides.

Also on iPhone

  • Russian, Ukrainian, Greek, Arabic, and Hebrew layouts, arranged as on Apple's keyboards.
  • Tap ΄ and then a vowel for ό. A Greek word ending in σ gets ς when you type a space.
  • In Hebrew and Arabic, dragging the space bar left moves toward the left of the line.
  • The keyboard, Lock Screen, and Control Center show Dictate in butter with the waves glyph.
  • Switching tabs shows the page at once, with no slide.
